findings: Western Region AS1, AS1J, L1, M1, CC/L1CC and handed variants, CS1/CS1S and S1N/S1O.
Dimensioned plans, seating depths and fixing relationships; concrete-sleeper chairs distinguished.
limitations: No complete jaw sections.
The sheet refers to SRE drawings; overlapping REA patterns are not independent design corroboration.
This is not a pre-grouping GWR standard.

sheets.title: Chairs (4)
findings: Old/new 3S, 4S and P switch-chair families, dimension tables and handing.
limitations: Amendment footer incompletely legible; visible issue date does not date every alteration.

sheets.title: Arrangement of Switch Chairs & Switch Blocks
findings: Switch-chair/block sequences for several switch lengths and types; stock-rail lengths and toe-opening table.
limitations: No complete timber-length schedule.

sheets.title: Dimensions of Switches (1), Old Type
findings: Old-type switches, 9–30 ft; chair-centre spacing, stretcher-bar locations, planing and stock/tongue lengths.
limitations: Positioning evidence, not every timber outline.

sheets.title: Arrangement of Crossing Chairs, Guards & Blocks
findings: Crossing-angle arrangements, including compounds; selected distances and an approximate timber-spacing note.
limitations: Rail section not explicitly stated; detailed chairs refer to R.1734–35.

sheets.title: Arrangement of Elbow Chairs
findings: Elbow/obtuse-chair placement and numerical tables for diamonds and single/double compounds.
limitations: Footer poorly legible; rail section not stated.
R.1780 chair-detail sheet was not examined.

sheets.title: Switch Stretcher Bars
findings: Several stretcher-bar designs, catchpoint applications, selected dimensions and component references.
limitations: Footer, date and some details poorly reproduced.
The staff notes direct readers to controlling standard drawings; they are not complete foundry drawings.
Concrete-sleeper chair coverage does not establish complete concrete-sleeper construction or spacing standards.
research_observations.reported_rights: The host home page carries a Keith Norgrove copyright notice. No item-specific permission to redistribute scans was established.

candidate_sources.title: British Railways Points and Crossings

locator.author: W. B. Worthington
locator.examined_proceedings: Compte rendu général, first volume, Brussels: P. Weissenbruch, 1901

research_observations.access: Free facsimile PDFs and online original-volume viewing reported.

findings: 1:8 common and obtuse crossing units, 24 ft points, numbered chair positions, base/weight table, timber centres and 1:20 inclination.
1:8 common crossing with timbers/checks, obtuse crossing, 12 ft check rail, wing-rail table and 18 ft points with 24 ft stock rails.
Whole double-slip rail geometry and multi-road crossover calculations.
Plate 35, figure 1: 1:8 crossings, 12 ft straight points and 628.62 ft radius.
limitations: No timber plan or chair schedule; company and rail section not stated.
Congress year 1900 differs from proceedings publication year 1901.
Some figures titled diamond crossing show the obtuse unit, not a complete diamond formation.
Assembly relationships do not supply every casting detail.
Modern Oldpway text transcription is distinct from the facsimile plates. CNAM and Oldpway copies of the same report are not independent corroboration.
research_observations.reported_rights: The report attributes to Oldpway a statement permitting copying/use of this plate collection for any purpose, with credit requested. The legal chain is not independently cleared. Modern scan borders/calibration marks and CNAM reproduction conditions remain distinct.
research_observations.optional_access_lead: The collection page offers enquiries about original drawings or greyscale scans; no enquiry is authorised here.

candidate_sources.title: Strengthening of Permanent Way in View of Increased Speed of Trains

locator.author: William Hunt
locator.congress: Fifth International Railway Congress, London, June 1895

findings: Figure 8: 30 ft rail arrangement, 9 ft sleepers, 4 ft 8½ in gauge and nonuniform numerical sleeper centres.

limitations: Some chair/key views show assembly without complete dimensioned casting detail.
Intermediate bays are larger; their small fractional labels remain untranscribed.

Plate and report are one publication, not separate independent confirmations.

research_findings: Reported LMS and GCR evidence ties sleeper spacing to rail joints and direction. Complete sequences and within-rail/across-joint distinctions matter; rail length divided by sleeper count is not a spacing rule.
Hunt’s company examples show several joint-support arrangements without establishing prevalence across all railways, a universal sequence or uniform within-rail spacing.

Timber lengths, staggering, chair allocation and dimensions remain tied to identified company, rail and formation. Rail geometry, a crossing unit, a part-arrangement and a complete timbering packet have different coverage.
LMS Nos.18/18A and 38 retain their qualified relationships to No.4 and the revised P-chair supersession. These relationships remain within one source family.
Drawing dates, cast lettering and retracing dates are distinct. A 1928 compilation can include the 1943 rider; matching S.I./S1 labels do not establish matching revisions.

Printed numerical dimensions take priority over uncalibrated scan measurements. Full-size labels, worn examples and modern annotations are not equivalent evidence. No.48’s clearance belongs to inspection-gauge design.
LMS, NERA, NRM and Western sheets may share SRE originals or ancestry. Multiple reproductions of the same original are not independent corroboration.
The report states that it uses no Templot-derived geometry or modelling algorithm. This attributed statement does not reclassify retained Templot lineage.

Prototype geometry, model adaptations and manufacturing compensation stay separate. Model rail/gauge/flangeway choices, simplifications, fit adjustments and process allowances are not supplied by these prototype drawings.
research_reports.scope: British bullhead plain line, chair and fitting families, switches, crossings, diamonds, crossovers, scissors, single/double slips, and sleeper/turnout timbering. S.I. remains a baseline component within this wider research scope.
